title: Inertial Mass Seismometer
creator: Hank R. & Claude Code
subject: Environmental Monitoring
description: A cutaway seismometer driven as a damped harmonic oscillator, showing ground position, mass position and their difference at once, with a stiffness control that destroys the recording to prove why soft suspensions are required.

learningObjectives: Explain how a suspended mass provides a stationary reference inside a moving frame.
Predict how changing the mass or the suspension stiffness changes the record.
Identify instrument ringing as a damping artefact rather than as ground motion.
Describe why force feedback flattens the instrument response across frequencies.
prerequisites: Chapter 11: Zhang Heng's seismoscope and the inertial-mass principle
Basic behaviour of a mass on a spring

keyQuestions: What quantity does a seismometer actually record?
Why does a stiff spring make the instrument useless?
What happens to a slow ground movement, like a creeping landslide?
Why do modern seismometers output a current rather than a displacement?
commonMisconceptions: The suspended mass is genuinely stationary rather than approximately so.
A seismometer records the ground's motion directly.
A heavier mass or a stiffer spring always makes a better instrument.
Ringing on a seismogram means aftershocks.
assessmentOpportunities: States that the recorded signal is frame position minus mass position.
Predicts and then measures the attenuation caused by a stiff suspension.
Distinguishes an underdamped instrument artefact from real ground motion.
